subject: 6BA5086EF7E2E1DCF1B4CEEC0DBB4B55
introduction: Twelver Shí‘ih Islam awaits the return of its twelfth Imam, hidden since the ninth century, as the Qá’im, “He Who shall arise”, who will fill the earth with justice. In 1848, before the Crown Prince and the clergy of Tabriz, the Báb declared, “I am the Qá’im Whose day all await.” This guide gathers that claim, the Bahá’í reading of the traditions (confused in their letter, fulfilled in their meaning), and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s statement that the hidden Imam never had a physical existence. The Gospels record the same collision between a people’s expectation and the one who came: “Shall Christ come out of Galilee?”, “we trusted that it had been he”, and Isaiah’s man of sorrows set against the hoped-for king.
questions: What did the Shí‘ihs of 1848 expect the Qá’im to be and do? In what sense do the readings say the Báb fulfilled it?
The readings call the traditions “confused” and also fulfilled. How can both be said?
Why does a promised deliverer so often come in a form his own people reject?

outside.why: “This is the Qá’im Whose day all await.” This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
“Verily, I am the Qá’im.” The question such a claim must meet: art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?
The Testimony of God has been manifested. But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth?
Examined before the Crown Prince and the divines. Shall Christ come out of Galilee? Search, and look: for out of Galilee ariseth no prophet.
Can this Cause be derived from the traditions? The disciples’ expectation, disappointed by the event: we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel.
The traditions are all confused. The words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end.
Contradictions in the hadith about the twelfth Imam. When Christ cometh, no man knoweth whence he is.
The twelfth Imam did not exist in the physical world. The kingdom of God cometh not with observation.
When the Qá’im appears. The day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.
Who shall know that He is the Qá’im. O Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee.

They themselves say that when the Qá’im speaks the chiefs of the earth will flee. The expected conqueror, and the one who came: he is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief. Why do peoples expect a victor and receive a sufferer?
Ponder what they say of the Qá’im and find them in error. Ye can discern the face of the sky; but can ye not discern the signs of the times?
The Qayyúm came, and the Qá’im stood at the Gate. He must increase, but I must decrease.
